scope.method: Opened actual German sailing-lexicon entries, checked related German course cards, and traced label leaders against the SVG generator anatomy. Browser layout review belongs to the root agent.

texts.rationale: Forward stay ends at the bow on the right of the mast. Vorstag is the fixed support in that direction.
Aft stay runs from masthead to the stern at left. Achterstag is the permanent support; Backstag would name a running backstay.
Two rigging members reach the deck on either side of the mast. Wanten correctly names the lateral supports and preserves the plural.
The transverse strut at mast height y=96 is the spreader pair. Mytilus explicitly uses Salinge as the plural; it is not Segel or Sailing.
The line along the mast is a sail-hoisting line. Fall is distinct from Dirk, Schot, and the separate mast-rake meaning of Fall.
The line from boom to cockpit/deck aft of the mast controls the mainsail through the boom. Generic Schot is valid and matches the card.
The diagonal control below the boom runs toward the lower mast, restraining boom rise. Baumniederholer is the UK sailing kicker/boom-vang meaning.
The line from high on the mast to the outer boom end supports the boom. This is Dirk, not the sail-hoisting Fall.
Stays and shrouds support the mast. The wording and category are correct; the draft’s sole Segelcrew URL lacks this entry, so the verified sources here replace it.

texts.de: Laufendes Gut: setzt und trimmt Segel
texts.rationale: Setzen und Trimmen describes the movable rigging’s principal functions. It is a concise category description rather than a claim that each displayed line directly moves sailcloth.

caption.en: Standing rigging holds the mast up. Running rigging moves.
caption.de: Stehendes Gut stützt den Mast. Laufendes Gut dient zum Setzen und Trimmen der Segel.
caption.rationale: Both categories match the same support/operation distinction used by the nautical dictionaries. Setzen and Trimmen clarify the very broad English moves without changing the intended teaching point.

texts.rationale: The upper corner near (292,50) is the sail head. Segelkopf is an explicit sailing compound also used by the existing card.
The lower forward corner near (292,254), next to the mast at right, is Hals. Tack does not name a turning manoeuvre here.
The lower aft corner near (114,258), away from the mast, is Schothorn.
The vertical forward edge between head and tack at x=292 is Vorliek; luff is an edge noun here.
The sloping aft edge from upper right to lower left is Achterliek. It is correctly on the left when the bow faces right.
The bottom edge between the two lower corners is Unterliek, not Fuß.
The separate upright spar at x=312 supports the sail; Mast matches the course term.
The separate spar under the sail extends aft from the mast. Baum is correct, with Großbaum as the more specific alternative taught in the card.

caption.en: Triangular mainsail, with the bow to the right.
caption.de: Dreieckiges Großsegel. Der Bug ist rechts.
caption.rationale: The SVG is a triangular mainsail aft of the mast. Its luff and mast are on the right, so the stated bow direction is correct.

findings.issue: The draft cites only https://segelcrew.at/lexikon/s for this occurrence, but its actual page has no Stehendes Gut entry.
findings.correction: Use https://www.mytilus.de/segellexikon.html, entry Stehendes Gut, as a checked sailing-lexicon source. The existing caption’s sportbootfuehrerschein.de reference also supports the claim.
